extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, academic departments/institutions, and advertisers using Notices of the AMS (for job advertising, classified ads, and book orders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines, rates, submission procedures, and content/format requirements for placing classified advertisements, requesting examination copies/adoptions, and ordering publications through the AMS Notices (March 1996 issue). Also includes typical job-application material & qualification expectations appearing in classified positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested uses for classified advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested uses for classified advertising are positions available, books or lecture notes for sale, books being sought, exchange or rental of houses, and typing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified ad rates and sizing (1995)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 1995 rate is $100 per inch or fraction thereof on a single column (one-inch minimum), calculated from top of headline. Any fractional text of 1/2 inch or more will be charged at the next inch rate. No discounts for multiple ads or the same ad in consecutive issues. For an additional $10 charge, announcements can be placed anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fractional text less than half an inch presumably not charged up; no member discounts for classified ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline formatting for 'Positions Available'
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements in the 'Positions Available' classified section will be set with a minimum one-line headline, consisting of the institution name above body copy, unless additional headline copy is specified by the advertiser. Headlines will be centered in boldface at no extra charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and dictation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads will appear in the language in which they are submitted. Dictation over the telephone will not be accepted for classified advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified advertisement deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Upcoming deadlines for classified advertising are as follows: May issue February 29, 1996; June issue-March 29, 1996; July issue-May 2, 1996; August issue-May 30, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers must meet the listed deadlines for placement in the corresponding issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination statement requirement for foreign institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. laws prohibit discrimination in employment on the basis of color, age, sex, race, religion, or national origin. 'Positions Available' advertisements from institutions outside the U.S. cannot be published unless they are accompanied by a statement that the institution does not discriminate on these grounds whether or not it is subject to U.S. laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and specific wording may be found near the Classified Advertisements in the January and July issues of the Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations-wanted (involuntarily unemployed) advertising policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations wanted advertisements from involuntarily unemployed mathematicians are accepted under certain conditions for free publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call toll-free 800-321-4AMS (321-4267) in the U.S. and Canada, or 401-455-4084 worldwide, for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels and billing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission: Promotions Department, AMS, P.O. Box 6248, Providence, Rhode Island 02940, or via fax, 401-331-3842, or send e-mail to classads@math.ams.org. AMS location for express delivery packages is 201 Charles Street, Providence, Rhode Island 02904.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers will be billed upon publication. Correspondence for anonymous announcements will be forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination copy / textbook adoption request requirements (Birkhäuser)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request an examination copy of a Birkhäuser textbook, please send your request on departmental letterhead and include the name of your course and current text, estimated class size, and the adoption decision date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination copies are shipped with an invoice payable in 30 days. Adopters may keep the copy free for desk use by returning the invoice with the bookstore and order size indicated. Others are required to remit payment or return the book. Send adoption examination requests to: Birkhäuser, Marketing Dept. Y048, address given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering/publication sales: shipping & payment terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for delivery are $3.00 per order, or for air delivery outside of the continental U.S., include $6.50 per item. Prepayment required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order from AMS P.O. Box 5904, Boston, MA 02206-5904. For credit-card orders fax (401) 331-3842 or call toll free 800-321-4AMS in U.S. and Canada. Residents of Canada, please include 7% GST. All prices subject to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering/territory and publisher-distribution notes (SMF series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles in this series are published by the Societe Mathematique de France and distributed by the AMS in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Orders from other countries should be sent to the SMF (Maison de la SMF or Institut Henri Poincaré addresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the SMF receive a 30% discount from list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical job-application materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should include items such as a letter of application, resume/CV or vita, names and addresses of references (often 3–5), transcripts, and arrangements for letters of recommendation to be sent (commonly three). Some postings request a statement of professional goals and a list of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific postings list exact materials and where to send them; many specify that at least one recommender address teaching experience. Applications often must be complete by a stated date to receive full consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical minimum qualifications for academic posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Many positions require a Ph.D. (completed by a given date) as a minimum qualification. Other common requirements include demonstrated excellence in teaching, evidence of successful teaching experience, research productivity, and strong interpersonal/communication skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some positions specify additional minimums (e.g., doctorate in mathematics or mathematical education, demonstrated ability to direct doctoral students, post-Ph.D. teaching years for ranks, or specialized technical backgrounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-specific preferred qualifications and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Postings frequently state preferences and duties such as emphasis in statistics or applied mathematics; ability to assist in initiation of undergraduate research program; background in use of technology in teaching; strength in stochastic calculus and financial mathematics; ability to work collaboratively with engineering/industry; or capacity to teach particular courses and supervise student research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank, salary, tenure eligibility, teaching load, and other responsibilities are specified per posting; some appointments may lead to tenure in an academic unit depending on qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review and deadline practice for positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of applications will begin on a stated date and will continue until the position is filled; screening/interviews may begin on specified dates; some postings state 'to receive full consideration, applications must be complete by [date]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some positions accept nominations and applications until filled; others have strict closing dates. Applicants are often told to send materials to a named contact or search committee address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration/nationality/eligibility notes in hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Some advertisements include immigration or citizenship-related preferences or restrictions (e.g., 'In accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada'; 'Candidates must be eligible for employment in the United States'; statements about U.S. passport restrictions for positions in certain countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check country- and institution-specific eligibility conditions before applying.
